## Things that depend on your setup

What changes with your PC, your equipment or REAPER's settings. Where it says “not tried”, the author has not tested it.

### Sound

- **Hearing the cue apart on headphones** needs an output other than the main one ([“Listening to a deck on headphones (Cue)”](listening-to-a-deck-on-headphones-cue.md)).
- **The video's audio**: only the first audio track of a video is imported. In a video with several (another language, a commentary), it may not be the one you want. 5.1 and other layouts are mixed down to stereo.
- **Sample rate**: the imported audio keeps the video's sample rate; when it differs from your audio interface's, it is converted as it plays. The length limit also depends on it (about 11.5 minutes for a 96 kHz video; see [“Step 1: Import a video”](basic-use.md#step-1-import-a-video)).
- **The deck's track**: a deck sounds while the `scratch engine` track's record arm and input monitoring are on. Turning either off, or muting the track in REAPER (`M`), stops not only the sound but also the loading of samples and the deck itself. To make it quieter, lower the track's fader instead.
- **Audio buffer**: a larger buffer means fewer dropouts but a later response to the jog. The video does not allow for the audio output's delay, so the larger the buffer, the later the sound is heard after the picture (how much has not been measured). A look-ahead limiter or the like on the master delays it the same way.
- **The headphone (Cue) output**: the chosen output is kept in the project by its number. If you open the project on another PC or with an audio device with fewer outputs and that output is not there, run setup again to choose anew. If the number exists but is now another jack, choose again under the `Cue` track's `ROUTE`.
- **If REAPER crashes**: with WaveOut as the audio system, a forced quit while playing once left the last sound looping on the Windows side. Playing another sound (a silent file, for example) on Windows' default output stopped it.

### Video

- **REAPER's video decoder order**: REAPER uses the decoders in the order of `Video decoder priority` under `Options` > `Preferences` > `Media` > `Video`. With the default order (`wmf vlc ffmpeg …`), the all-intra AVI (MJPEG) files were also read by WMF, and seeking was about 3 times slower than with FFmpeg. WMF sometimes showed an mp4's picture 2 frames off. If REAPER can use its FFmpeg decoder, putting `ffmpeg:avi` first reads only AVI files with FFmpeg (for example `ffmpeg:avi wmf vlc ffmpeg qt:mov,qt,m4v,mp4`). Turning on `Show decoder information` on the same page shows in the video window which decoder is used.
- **The video cache setting**: with `All media and video FX are not cached`, which setup recommends, other scripts running in REAPER (visualizers and the like) may slow down while a heavy video effect such as VHS is on.
- **Frame rates and large files**: a 60 fps video is heavier than 30 fps and its converted file larger (not tried). Videos with a variable frame rate (from a phone, for example) and converted files over 2 GB have not been tried either. If it is heavy, cut the video shorter or choose a smaller conversion height in setup.
- **Screen size**: the JSFX screen grows only in whole multiples with its window. The kit's window layout was made on a 1920×1080 screen. On a smaller screen or with display scaling (125%, 150% …), windows may fall off the screen (not tried). Move them and save the window set again.
- **External screens on a laptop**: on laptops whose external screen ports are wired to an NVIDIA (or other) GPU, the GPU driver's processing grew long enough to cause dropouts. Setting `reaper.exe` to “High-performance NVIDIA processor” with power management “Prefer maximum performance” in the NVIDIA Control Panel fixed it (at the cost of more heat and power). Which port goes to which GPU differs between models.
- **Capturing with OBS**: OBS's “Window Capture” could not capture a floating JSFX window. Use “Display Capture” and crop.

### Controllers and keyboard

- **Other devices and programs**: a deck listens to all MIDI inputs. If another MIDI device (a keyboard, a foot switch …), ReaLearn, a REAPER control surface or an action shortcut uses the same channel and number, the deck moves too. Disable the inputs a deck does not need in REAPER's MIDI inputs. On Windows, REAPER may not be able to use a controller that rekordbox, Serato, Traktor or another DJ program is using (not tried). Quit that program first.
- **Two of the same unit, or plugged in again**: the lights go to the first output found by the preset's name, so with two of the same unit they may go to the other one. When the name or number of a MIDI output changes (another USB port, for example), run setup again.
- **The light-off helper (Windows)**: to turn the lights off after REAPER closes, the video sync starts PowerShell in a hidden window. On a work or school PC, or with some antivirus software, it may be blocked and the lights stay on (not tried; REAPER itself is not affected). The helper sends 0 for every note and CC on all channels of the light outputs. If those outputs go to another program through loopMIDI or the like, that program's volume (CC7) and so on go to 0 too.
- **Keyboard layouts**: the keys are laid out for a Japanese keyboard. For `Shift`+`7` on an English keyboard, see the keys under [“Step 3: Scratch”](basic-use.md#step-3-scratch). German, French and other layouts, an input method (IME) that is on, and F1–F8 on a Mac laptop (which may need the Fn key) have not been tried.
- **The HID bridge (Mac)**: if asked for Input Monitoring permission, allow it (not tried).

### REAPER and the PC

- **REAPER version**: tested with REAPER 7.80 (the template was saved with 7.82). With older versions the JSFX may not load, the length limit may be shorter, or a menu in this manual may be missing. Systems other than Windows and macOS (Linux) have not been tried.
- **REAPER-wide settings that setup changes**: with the SWS extension installed, setup turns off `Limit scrub rate to 1.0x` on the `Scrub/Jog` page of `Preferences`. This applies to all projects (tick it again to undo). When toolbar 3 or a window set is replaced, the old content is kept in `reaper-menu.ini.before_reascratch` and `reaper-screensets.ini.before_reascratch` in REAPER's resource folder. To go back, close REAPER and replace the file with its copy, taking `.before_reascratch` off the name (later changes to menus or window sets are undone too).
- **Updating the kit**: after copying a new kit over the old one, restart REAPER. A running video sync and open JSFX keep the old version until then.
- **Moving the kit or REAPER's resource folder**: the autostart lines (`__startup.lua`) and the toolbar buttons remember where the kit is. If that changes (for example, a portable REAPER on a USB stick gets another drive letter), run setup again (when the autostart cannot start the sync, REAPER's console says so).
- **Starting the video sync again and again**: starting it again from an action several times once brought up REAPER's “ReaScript task control” window, which kept coming back after closing. Restart REAPER then.
- **Power and memory**: run a laptop on its AC adapter with a high-performance power setting. On battery or power saving it is heavier and drops out more easily (the author's PC runs REAPER on its fast cores, so other PCs may be heavier). Long samples can use up to about 1 GB of memory per deck (not measured).

### Where files go

- **Imported sound and captures**: imported sound (WAV) is kept in `Data/ReaScratch_samples` in REAPER's resource folder, captures in `Data/ReaScratch_takes`. While a capture makes its video, images of every frame are also made there for a while. Check the free space on the drive that holds the resource folder (usually C:).
- **Opening a project on another PC**: the JSFX remembers samples by their filenames in `ReaScratch_samples`. If you move only the .rpp to another PC or reinstall REAPER, the samples show `ERR`. Move the files in `Data/ReaScratch_samples` with it.
- **Where the all-intra video goes**: into the original video's folder (about 100 MB per minute at 720p). It fails in a read-only place. In a folder synced by OneDrive or the like, uploading the large file may go on during the show. Copy the video to a working folder before converting.
- **Folder names and usernames**: Japanese characters and spaces in filenames have been tried. A PC with a Japanese Windows username has not.
